title: Lahaina Disaster Recovery Update Meeting of January 10, 2024

issues.title: MEMA community resiliency hub network plan

recap.headline: Lahaina recovery update: debris removal start, checkpoints, housing and new recovery office
recap.in_60_seconds: Mayor Bissen and county, state, federal and nonprofit partners gave their weekly Lahaina recovery update. Twelve officials and three people speaking for organizations presented, and no residents spoke from the floor; questions went to tables afterward. The Army Corps said Lahaina residential debris removal is ready to start with 5 properties, growing to as many as 35 teams, once the County Council finishes its review of the Olowalu temporary debris site. The county reported over 1,800 of about 2,100 rights of entry submitted, and SBA said its loan application grace period ends January 25. Red Cross said Honua Kai shelter guests told to move can stay for now, and a new county Office of Recovery will build a long-term recovery plan with community input. A housing update from the Mayor's Advisory Team was promised for January 31.

parts.title: Welcome and introductions
presented: Thanked county and state crews for storm response in recent days
Acknowledged the West Maui councilmember in attendance
Introduced the new Maui Emergency Management Agency administrator, a retired fire battalion chief

parts.title: Maui Emergency Management Agency update and checkpoint passes
presented: The agency has many vacancies and is focused on filling them
MEMA is building a Maui incident management team to support field and emergency operations center work
Plans to replicate the 12 community-run distribution points from the West Maui response, which served about 6,000 people a day with about 2,500 volunteers, so government plugs in faster
A private security company replaced the National Guard at checkpoints; passes speed entry, keep out people who do not belong and add safety during debris removal

next.what: Pass issuance resumes at the Disaster Recovery Center Monday, Wednesday and Friday 8 to 4 and Saturday 8 to 2

parts.title: Checkpoint security company introduction
presented: Both owners described long local careers in police and hotel security
Staff were asked to show compassion and empathy at checkpoints
Acknowledged complaints after stopping everyone during the transition and said they aim to reduce intrusion as they get to know residents

parts.title: FEMA housing and Army Corps debris and school update
parts.presenter: FEMA representative; Army Corps of Engineers colonel
presented: FEMA has 1,296 households available in its direct lease program, 76 leased in so far, and seeks owners to lease units for up to 24 months
The temporary debris storage site held up in the storm; runoff came from road construction, not the containment cell
The temporary school near Kapalua Airport is targeted for late February so students can move in for the fourth quarter; Kula and Olinda debris work, about 25 properties, is substantially complete
Lahaina residential debris removal will start with 5 properties and add about 5 teams every two weeks, up to as many as 35 teams

next.what: County Council final review of using the Olowalu temporary debris storage site, after which Lahaina debris removal begins

parts.title: Health, small business loans, air monitoring and insurance
parts.presenter: U.S. Health and Human Services representative; SBA public information officer; State Department of Health deputy director; State Insurance Division representative
presented: HHS offers free, confidential behavioral health support and is shifting it to a state crisis counseling program hiring local counselors; a new playground is coming to the temporary school
SBA loans: renters up to $100,000 and homeowners up to $500,000 for uninsured losses; people referred by FEMA must complete the SBA application to stay eligible for other FEMA aid
Department of Health has installed 65 PurpleAir sensors in Lahaina and will monitor air during debris work, as it did in Kula
Insurers have paid over $1 billion in claims with about half a billion more reserved; residents can call the Insurance Division at 808-586-2790

next.what: SBA disaster loan application grace period ends

parts.title: Red Cross shelter update for Honua Kai
parts.presenter: Speaker for Red Cross and the Mayor's Advisory Team
presented: Honua Kai guests told to relocate this week can stay, since those properties will not join the program moving people from condos to hotels
Red Cross shelters almost 6,000 people at 36 sites and apologized for the confusion
Honua Kai contracts vary; the earliest end date is January 31

next.what: Guests in rooms with a January 31 end date will be notified
Mayor's Advisory Team presents on housing at the community meeting
Disaster Recovery Center closed for Martin Luther King Day

parts.title: Rights of entry for debris removal
presented: Over 1,800 of about 2,100 rights of entry submitted; a gap of a little over 300 remains
One Gmail address can now cover multiple properties, and any insurance document with name, address and policy number is accepted
Commercial properties are eligible; please do not pull ineligible debris into the road
Working with state courts on an expedited process when the owner has died

next.what: Right-of-entry workshop at Lahainaluna cafeteria, 3 to 5:30 p.m.

parts.title: New county Office of Recovery
presented: The County Council approved funding and positions, and a recovery management contractor will help secure all available federal funding
A public sentiment analysis and recovery needs assessment will feed a long-term recovery plan the community will help prioritize
Six recovery teams follow the National Disaster Recovery Framework: housing, infrastructure, health and social services, natural and cultural resources, economic recovery and community planning
Weekly meetings will shift toward engagement and outreach

next.what: Community meeting schedule for recovery engagement announced

parts.title: Mayor's closing remarks
presented: Five of nine MEMA positions were vacated since August; four remain to fill
The MEMA administrator scored highest among 15 applicants and 5 finalists tested by other emergency management directors
Recovery teams are staffed by two county department leaders each, plus Lahaina advisory members and partners
This is about the ninth or tenth weekly Lahaina meeting, with similar Tuesday meetings in Kula

parts.title: Closing reminders
presented: Presenters available at back tables for individual questions
Right-of-entry workshop reminder for Saturday at Lahainaluna cafeteria, 3 to 5:30 p.m.

bills.name: Olowalu temporary debris storage site approval
bills.what: County Council final review allowing the Army Corps to use the Olowalu site to hold Lahaina fire debris.

bills.name: National Disaster Recovery Framework
bills.what: Federal model the county uses to organize its six recovery teams.

bills.name: Lahaina long-term recovery plan
bills.what: Plan to be developed from the needs assessment and community input to guide recovery projects.

not_on_tracker.topic: Lahaina debris removal and rights of entry
not_on_tracker.why: Property owners must submit a right of entry before crews can clear their lots, and about 300 are still missing.
Residents going to their properties now pass a private security company that replaced the National Guard.

not_on_tracker.topic: Red Cross shelter relocations at Honua Kai
not_on_tracker.why: Displaced families were told to move and then told they could stay, with some contracts ending January 31.

moments.who: Acting County Managing Director leading the Office of Recovery
moments.quote: That recovery needs assessment will be used to develop strategies and implementing projects that will be able to actually undertake a lot of the recovery efforts that our community has desired.
moments.about: Explains that a recovery needs assessment, built from community testimony, would feed the strategies and projects in the recovery plan.

moments.who: Acting County Managing Director leading the Office of Recovery
moments.quote: As a part of this whole process, we'll develop a long-term recovery plan that will help to guide the efforts of all of our projects and partners.
moments.about: In January 2024, the county said a long-term recovery plan would guide all recovery projects and partners and would include community feedback.

moments.who: Acting County Managing Director leading the Office of Recovery
moments.quote: And you know, as one example of a culturally significant site like Mokuʻula and working And we're working with the community on how that's envisioned and the project and plan to set forth for that area.
moments.about: Shows that Mokuʻula was named early in recovery planning as a cultural site whose future plan would be shaped with the community.
